messages:
maya: Nightly eval popped a consistent regression on the "anchor" prompt set after pushing v2.4.0 (weights + tokenizer). Accuracy down ~18% vs v2.3.0. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/nightly/anchor_promptset

ci-bot: Nightly job 2026-03-19 03:12 finished. Regression detected: anchor_promptset_accuracy decreased 18% (p=0.006). See artifacts: s3://redwood/nightly/v2.4.0/compare.zip

adrien: Can you drop one of the failing examples? We need a minimal repro to triage quickly.

maya: repro below (trimmed). Notice weird token boundary and repeated punctuation in the gen: 
```
INPUT: "Summarize the following agreement and highlight obligations for the supplier."
REFERENCE: bullet points
OUTPUT(v2.3.0): "- Supplier must deliver X within 30 days; - Supplier responsible for QA; ..."
OUTPUT(v2.4.0): "- Supplier must deliver X within 30 days ;;
- Supplier responsible for QA"
```

samir: That double-semicolon looks like a token boundary artifact. I pulled tokenization of the offending span: new tokenizer splits the em-dash and merges some hyphenated forms differently. Possibly a BPE merging table reorder.

eva: I ran a quick local run: same prompt, old weights + new tokenizer -> drop still present. New weights + old tokenizer -> also drop but smaller (~6%). So both changed but tokenizer change is the larger delta.

liam: I diffed token_to_id between v2.3.0 and v2.4.0. Example: the token " -" (space+hyphen) id is 432 in v2.3.0 and 431 in v2.4.0; a lot of off-by-one shifts across the tail of vocab. Suspect we rebuilt merges with different ordering which shifted indices and serialization mapping.

adrien: If token IDs moved but weights expect old embedding ordering we could get subtle index mismatch during serialization/compat. Are embeddings being remapped on model load?

maya: Loader logs show a conversion step, but it assumes stable BPE->id mapping. I pasted the conversion log excerpt: 
```
INFO: loading tokenizer vocabulary v2.4.0
INFO: applying merge table
INFO: writing idmap.bin (created 50224 entries)
```
No explicit remap step for embeddings in the artifact build.

samir: That explains behavioral drift. If embeddings stayed in the old index order but tokenizer produces new ids, tokens will hit wrong vectors -> semantic drift and punctuation weirdness.

eva: Workaround options:
- rollback tokenizer to v2.3 in the v2.4 release bundle (fast)
- add an embedding id-remap at load-time (safer but takes engineering)
- serve v2.4 but route anchor_promptset traffic to v2.3 variant (canary routing)

liam: I prepared a small patch that injects an id_remap.json during model build when we detect reorder. Quick diff: 
```json
{"old_to_new": {"432":431, "433":432}}
```
This remap fixes the repro locally for me. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/emb-remap/pull/12

adrien: Good, but we need test coverage. Add a nightly unit test that runs the anchor prompt set and asserts top-k tokens for guarded spans. Also add a check in the build pipeline to fail if token_to_id histogram shift > 0.5% for high-frequency tokens.

maya: Filing issue and linking artifacts: https://issues.redwood/ML-2984 — includes reproducer, dump of token_to_id diffs, local fix patch, comparison graphs, and suggested rollback plan for canary.

ci-bot: Created issue ML-2984 and assigned to eng-ml.

samir: I'll coordinate a hotfix: push remap to the v2.4 artifact and re-run the nightly canary suite. If that passes, we'll promote. If not, rollback tokenizer to v2.3 for v2.4 release and schedule a deeper compatibility redesign.

eva: I'll add the anchor prompt golden checks and the build-time histogram guard.

maya: Thanks — I'll notify eng-runtime to pause wide rollout and schedule a 12:00 UTC canary re-run. @eng-runtime FYI. :thumbsup:

liam: Created the canary job: job/emb-remap-canary-2156789. Link: https://ci.redwood/builds/emb-remap-canary-2156789

maya: Closing loop here once canary completes. Appreciate the quick triage team.
